get.summary: Show compliance information for a Work Order Contract
get.description: Return the compliance and insurance information for the specified contract. Includes any insurance documents for the vendor on this contract.

parameters.name: contract_id
parameters.description: identifier for the work order contract

updated_at.description: The last time the any of this compliance information was updated on this contract

updated_by_id.description: The last user who updated this compliance information

compliance_status.description: The compliance status of this contract

compliance_notes.description: Any notes about the compliance status

insurance_status.description: The insurance status of this contract

insurance_notes.description: Any notes about the insurance status

derived_insurance_status.description: A computed status based on the insurance documents for this contract's vendor. If all documents are compliant, this will be compliant. If any documents are not compliant, this will be not_compliant. If there are no documents, this will be the insurance status field on the contract.

id.description: The identifier of the insurance record

name.description: The name of the insurance record

insurance_type.description: The type of the insurance record

level.description: Whether this insurance record is attached in the company or project directory

status.description: The compliance status of this insurance document

effective_at.description: The time which this insurance becomes effective. This time is the effective_date in the project or companies timezone converted to UTC.

expires_at.description: The time which this insurance expires. This time is the expiration_date in the project or companies timezone converted to UTC.

attachments.description: the files attached to this insurance record

content_type.description: the content type of the file

url.description: a signed URL to load the file

derived_compliance_status.description: A computed status based on the compliance documents for this contract. If all documents are compliant, this will be compliant. If any documents are not compliant, this will be not_compliant. If there are no documents, this will be the compliance status field on the contract.

content_type.description: the content type of the file

url.description: a signed URL to load the file

level.description: The level of the insurance requirement

status.description: The status of the insurance requirement

compliance_requirements_not_created.description: Compliance requirements that have conditions but are not yet created

id.description: The identifier of the compliance requirement

name.description: The name of the compliance requirement

x-code-samples.title: Node.js
Python3
x-code-samples.content:
import http.client

conn = http.client.HTTPSConnection("api.procore.com")

headers = { 'Authorization': "Bearer REPLACE_BEARER_TOKEN" }

conn.request("GET", "/rest/v1.0/projects/%7Bproject_id%7D/work_order_contracts/%7Bcontract_id%7D/compliance", headers=headers)

res = conn.getresponse()
data = res.read()

print(data.decode("utf-8"))

x-changelog.summary: Promote commitment compliance endpoints to general availability (GA)
x-changelog.description:
The commitment compliance endpoints were previously in beta (`commitment-compliance-api-beta`) and have now been made publicly available (`visibility: public`).
No changes were made to the API contract, only visibility updates.

x-changelog.summary: Add requirements not created fields to commitment compliance response
x-changelog.description:
Added two new fields to the commitment compliance response to show requirements that have conditions but are not yet created:
- `insurance_requirements_not_created`: Array of insurance requirements with conditions that haven't been created yet
- `compliance_requirements_not_created`: Array of compliance requirements with conditions that haven't been created yet

Each requirement includes an `id`, `name`, `status` (always "condition_not_met"), and either `level` (for insurance) or `type` (for compliance).

Python3
x-code-samples.content:
import http.client

conn = http.client.HTTPSConnection("api.procore.com")

payload = "{\"compliance_status\":\"compliant\",\"compliance_notes\":\"string\",\"insurance_status\":\"compliant\",\"insurance_notes\":\"string\"}"

headers = {
    'Authorization': "Bearer REPLACE_BEARER_TOKEN",
    'content-type': "application/json"
    }

conn.request("PATCH", "/rest/v1.0/projects/%7Bproject_id%7D/work_order_contracts/%7Bcontract_id%7D/compliance", payload, headers)

res = conn.getresponse()
data = res.read()

print(data.decode("utf-8"))
